newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Kabila aide calls for popular uprising in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Kabila aide calls for popular uprising in Zaire.

text.p: A spokesman for Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Sunday called on other political groups in Zaire to organise an uprising against the regime of president Mobutu Sese Seko and speed up the ailing president's fall.

"The oppostion parties, UDPS and others, should, along with other organisations, accelerate the fall of Mobutu instead of waiting until Kabila arrives in Kinshasa," Muteba Tshitenge, a Brussels-based spokesman for Kabila's Alliance for Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo/Zaire (AFDL), said.

"Everywhere, in Lubumbashi and elsewhere, do not wait for Kabila. There must be a popular uprising, which must overtake all the big cities," Tshitenge said in a debate with other Zairean opposition parties on Belgian RTBF television.
Kabila's forces have captured about a fifth of Zaire's territory in the east of the vast central African country, including Kisangani, the country's third city.
They are now heading for southern Lubumbashi, the second-biggest city, and the capital Kinshasa.
Representatives of several other Zairean parties, who all have headquarters in Belgium, Zaire's former colonial ruler, agreed Mobutu has to go, but hesitated to call for mass rallies.

"We must push for Mobutu to step down. He cannot be included in any solution about the future of Zaire," said Justine Kasa-Vubu, Brussels-based spokeswoman for Etienne Tshisekedi's Union for Democracy and Social Progress (UDPS), Zaire's main opposition party.
But she did not reply to Tshitenge's call.
"Politicians in Kinshasa must contribute so that we can sit around the table and find a solution," she said.

Albert M'Peti, Brussels-based spokesman for Zaire's Democratic Christian Social Party (PDSC), was less evasive: "To call mass rallies would be irresponsible. What remains of the military forces of this dying regime is completely cornered and desperate. To send people in the streets means risking carnage," he said.
Tshitenge avoided questions about whether Kabila's AFDL was willing to start talks with the UDPS about a post-Mobutu Zaire.
"After the war Mobutu-Kabila, I can see a crisis between Kabila and Tshisekedi," one of the participants in the debate said.

On Saturday Kabila said he was willing to cooperate with other political movements in Zaire in a transitional government, but only with anti-Mobutist forces who have never shared power with the ailing president.
Mobutu, 66, on Friday returned home from France, where he was recovering from cancer treatment.
Tshitenge rejected Western calls for talks with Mobutu.
"How can Europe ask us to make a democracy with Mobutu. He has killed people, he is a criminal with whom we cannot build a democracy," he said.
